source.title: Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity
source.authors: Mark Schöne; Babak Rahmani; Heiner Kremer; Fabian Falck; H. Ballani; J. Gladrow

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures held-out pretraining perplexity and downstream task performance across model sizes, but does not fit or test a power-law scaling relation.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports held-out D-Pile perplexity and downstream scores for model sizes from 130M to 1.3B. The perplexity results are relevant to parameter scaling, but the paper does not fit a power law or make small-run loss predictions. The downstream aggregate results are means across tasks; individual downstream task scores are also reported but are not separately cataloged here. Other scaling-law claims discussed in the related-work section are citations, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The four-size sweeps provide descriptive evidence on V6 in implicit and explicit language models: average downstream accuracy increases at every size transition in all six configurations. They do not establish the power-law form in V1 or quantitative downstream prediction.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate but should avoid an unconditional perplexity advantage: implicit models improve over explicit baselines in many cases, particularly on HellaSwag, while gains vary by task and configuration. For example, 130M Mamba2 (4+1) has worse perplexity than Mamba2* (13.76 versus 13.05). Self-iteration adds cost that the authors suggest may amortize chiefly on demanding state-tracking problems. Their central conclusion also concerns implicit SSMs acquiring nonlinear recurrent transitions and solving hard state-tracking problems.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains implicit Mamba2 and Llama variants with self-iteration and compares their held-out perplexities across sizes; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family and implicit training configuration are varied; no sensitivity analysis of scaling-law fitting choices is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Implicit versus explicit models differ in perplexity and downstream accuracy at nominally matched parameter scales, while self-iteration adds computation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive self-iteration can improve parameter efficiency, with benefits depending on model configuration and task.

fits_no_version.finding: Longer-context evaluation, convergence diagnostics and simultaneous/sequential agreement concern context generalization and implicit-model execution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Implicit models can improve context-length robustness and permit approximately equivalent parallel and sequential evaluation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The parameter sweep spans 130M to 1.3B, uses a fixed 207B-token training budget, and reports no fitted power law or prediction error. Table 1 gives no uncertainty estimates for the language-model perplexity or downstream scores.
record.rows_left_out: Individual downstream task scores from Table 1 are not included; the table's reported average downstream accuracy is retained for each model and size. Original Mamba2 and Llama baselines trained on different corpora/token budgets are omitted from the parameter-sweep rows. The D-Pile perplexity entries for Llama (32+4)-ours are not stated in the flattened Table 1 text and are not inferred.

untested.parts: Power-law functional form, exponents, several orders of magnitude, non-bottleneck conditions, and independent token or compute scaling. The parameter sweep spans approximately one order of magnitude.
Small-run fits predicting losses of substantially larger runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation under fixed compute budgets and its scaling exponents.
A controlled depth/width or architecture-shape sweep over a wide range. Explicit/implicit comparisons also change self-iteration and training computation.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes; implicit text pretraining alone does not establish this.
Quantitative prediction errors, held-out scale predictions, extrapolation beyond the tested sizes, and a predictive mapping from pretraining loss to downstream performance.
Sensitivity of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations to setup and fitting choices, and departures from a fitted single power law.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict follows from monotonic perplexity alone: the study supplies relevant measurements but does not determine the claimed functional form. Perplexity is exp(cross-entropy), so a power law in loss must not be inferred directly from a perplexity trend. Individual downstream scores are explicitly declared omitted and therefore are not missing extraction entries. Table 1 and Table 6 conflict systematically on Llama perplexity assignments; the supplied text cannot resolve those assignments.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports loss across parameter counts, but does not test a power-law fit, token-count or compute scaling, bottleneck conditions, or scaling over several orders of magnitude.
The paper reports downstream scores across model sizes, but does not predict downstream scores from smaller runs or from pretraining loss.

relationships.condition: Seven-task average accuracy within each of the six configurations, nominally 130M–1.3B parameters, after 207B D-Pile tokens
relationships.reason: A01–A24 show monotonic average-accuracy improvements at every size transition in all six series; this supports the within-range trend, without establishing numerical predictability or individual-task monotonicity.
relationships.display_finding: Seven-task average accuracy improved at every size transition in all six configurations, without establishing predictability or monotonic gains on individual tasks.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported parameter-size sweeps at fixed 207B training tokens, within the tested model families
reader_labels.reason: D-Pile test perplexity decreases across the reported size sweep for the Mamba2 and Llama configurations; this supports the direction of the trend but does not establish a power-law shape (rows P01–P20).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported average downstream accuracy across sizes, averaged over the seven tasks
reader_labels.reason: The reported averages generally rise across the tested sizes for the listed model series; the study does not establish predictive fits from small runs (rows A01–A24).
